svg.aria-label: What AutoCommand sends about you: nothing by default, three narrow lookups, everything else local

g.text: What it sends about you: nothing, by default
What can leave the machine
IP ownership — automatic, HTTPS only
unknown destination IPs are asked at public RDAP
registries, so rows say "Akamai", not bare numbers.
The registry learns the queried IP. That's the payload.
Sysmon64.exe — only when you click Install
downloaded from live.sysinternals.com and fully
Authenticode-verified before it is ever run.
Secure-boot DBX blob — only from Shields Up
Microsoft's revocation list, over HTTPS.
Plus one opt-in anonymous daily count — app, version,
Windows build. No identifier of any kind. Off unless asked.
What stays on your machine
Every connection, spawn, block and verdict — recorded
in readable local files (Technical Notes lists them all).
Decrypted request/response bodies, when you intercept
TLS, are DPAPI-encrypted at rest — your user, only —
while the metadata index stays greppable plaintext.
No account. No cloud middleman. The counting server
(if you opted in) stores daily totals — no per-user rows
exist anywhere in the system.
Changing your mind: withdraw consent in Settings, or
delete one registry key. Uninstalling removes it entirely.
Verify, don't trust: the counting worker's code is public in the repository, and PRIVACY.md spells out every lookup.
